title: Encoded and non-genetic protein variants expand human functional proteome.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: PRIDE project PXD073135 (CC0, public 2026-01-22): listed 86 files, 82 RAW (~0.5-0.7 GB each) plus 4 search tables (Hb, PRDX6, PARK7, GAPDH psm.tsv). Opened PRDX6_psm.tsv: 5,671 PSMs (peptide-spectrum matches) x 49 FragPipe columns; protein field encodes variant peptides like DINAYNCEEPTEK_Y4C. These are only the purified-protein validation runs. bioRxiv v1 and v2 supplement zips ('all supplementary tables') exist but both returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on download, so the main variant table was NOT opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 13,910 localized variants / 7,215 unique substitutions (abstract); per-variant log10 MS1 substitution-to-reference abundance ratio, RNA-seq-based genetic vs non-genetic call, MSFragger + PepQuery2 pipeline with ~2% estimated FDR, source raw data PXD010154 (29 tissues) and E-MTAB-2836 RNA-seq (bioRxiv full text). Preprint also cites 76,516 validated / 37,522 quantified / 46,046 unique position-substitutions at other filter stages. Nature supplement not checked (paywalled publisher site).

a1_downloadable.note: No login: PRIDE PXD073135 is CC0 and downloaded fine; bioRxiv supplement zip is public but returned HTTP 429 twice, so the main table is unverified, not blocked.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Per the preprint, the per-variant log10 substitution abundance ratio and genetic/non-genetic class are reported per substitution; not seen in files. A detected/not-detected label for unobserved positions would have to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Variants are peptide sequence + position + Ensembl v112 protein; full protein sequences need one bulk Ensembl FASTA, not thousands of lookups (paper only).

a4_units_stated.note: Label is a unitless log10 MS1 intensity ratio (substituted/reference), per the methods text; not checked in the table.

a5_enough_rows.note: 13,910 variants / 7,215 unique substitutions from the abstract; not counted in files. Preprint mentions up to 37,522 quantified substitutions at a looser filter.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <100 MB expected for supplementary tables (unverified); raw data PXD010154 is TB-scale and not needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tabular variant table plus ESM-2 embeddings of a few thousand proteins fits 16 GB CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Unverified: preprint quotes 76,516 / 37,522 / 46,046 at different filtering stages vs 13,910 / 7,215 in the abstract; must check which set the supplement contains.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a mass-spec measurement (MS1 intensity ratio) after search-engine identification at ~2% FDR, not another model's prediction; genetic vs non-genetic class is a rule from RNA-seq read counts, not from the sequence features we'd use.

B1.why: Supplement is a zip of several tables (paper text); not opened, keys assumed to be gene/position.

B2.why: Unknown; likely xlsx tables from a bioRxiv zip. PRIDE psm.tsv parsed first try.

B3.why: One pipeline, one lab's processing of one 29-tissue dataset; ratios computed uniformly (paper text).

B4.why: Ratios span 1e-7 to 1e2; undetected reference or substituted peptides likely yield missing ratios (paper text).

B5.why: Same substitution recurs across tissues/individuals (13,910 vs 7,215 unique); needs a collapse rule.

B6.why: Methods describe the quantities; column documentation unseen.

C1.why: Transfer test to Slavov-lab substitution set is informative either way; sequence-to-ratio model alone needs a signal to mean anything.

C2.why: Searches found descriptive analyses (Mordret 2019, Tsour 2026) but no predictive model of per-site substitution levels.

C3.why: Novel: nobody has trained a model on human mistranslation/non-genetic substitution measurements.

C4.why: Detection needs deep proteomics plus heavy cluster search; prediction from sequence would be cheap.

C5.why: Obvious dummies: per-substitution-type mean (e.g. near-cognate codon class); no published predictive number.

D1.why: ESM-2 protein language model, open weights, applies to protein sequence windows around each site.

D2.why: A few thousand proteins; embeddings cacheable once on CPU.

D3.why: ESM-2 MIT licence; PRIDE data CC0; bioRxiv preprint CC BY-NC.

E1.why: Hold out whole genes, or cluster proteins by sequence identity; gene IDs expected in tables.

E2.why: Thousands of genes and 29 tissues give many held-out groups (paper text).

E3.why: Per-substitution-type mean ratio and per-gene mean are trivial baselines.

E4.why: Same substitution measured across tissues/individuals gives replicate spread; not yet computed.

E5.why: Known effect: near-cognate codon mispairing (e.g. GGC Gly to Asp) should dominate, per Mordret 2019.

E6.why: Label shuffling and feature-block ablation (codon vs ESM vs expression) are straightforward.

E7.why: Tsour et al. 2026 Nature (Slavov lab) has 8,746 unique substitutions with open code/data site.

E8.why: Paper reports correlations, not a predictive benchmark to reproduce.

G1.why: Ensembl protein IDs plus residue positions expected (Ensembl v112 search database, paper text).

G2.why: Tsour et al. substitution set; AlphaFold DB structures; gnomAD allele frequencies, joined on gene + position.

G3.why: Ensembl-to-UniProt isoform mapping and position offsets need care.

G4.why: Whether structure/conservation predicts tolerated non-genetic substitutions across two labs is a modest new question.

H1.why: Only detected substitutions are recorded; non-detection is confounded with peptide detectability.

H2.why: 29 tissues but one source dataset (Wang 2019 atlas, PXD010154) and one lab's pipeline.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below, limited to detectable tryptic peptides.

H4.why: Detectability bias is inherent to the method; partly discussed via low-expression preference.

I1.why: Pilpel (Weizmann) and Slavov (Northeastern) labs; translation-fidelity community.

I2.why: Could prioritise sites for targeted validation, but marginal decision change.

I3.why: Spearman on held-out genes roughly matches prioritising sites for validation.

I4.why: Codon near-cognate rules may explain most variance; ML may add little.

J2.why: Mass-spec artefacts (PTMs mimicking substitutions) are hard to judge without proteomics expertise.

J3.why: A harmonised two-lab substitution table is useful even if the model fails.

J4.why: Two weeks plausible but not yet stated.

J5.why: Kill condition below, date not yet in NOTES.md.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model), 150M or 650M checkpoint, per-residue embeddings at each substituted site
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU; a few thousand proteins in under a few hours

integration.partner_dataset: Tsour et al. 2026 Nature (Slavov lab) alternate-decoding substitutions (8,746 unique sites, 26 tissues + 6 cancers); AlphaFold DB structures
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Are the sites where proteins carry non-genetic substitutions predictable from codon, structure and evolutionary tolerance, consistently across two independent detection pipelines?

controls.positive_control: Near-cognate codon substitutions (single-base codon-anticodon mismatches, e.g. Gly GGC to Asp) should rank highest; reported by Mordret 2019 in bacteria/yeast.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle ratios within substitution type and confirm collapse to per-type mean; ablate ESM features.
controls.external_validation: Tsour et al. 2026 substitution set from the Slavov lab (different pipeline, overlapping and additional tissues).

honest_claim_h3: Among single amino acid substitutions detectable by tryptic-peptide mass spectrometry in the Wang 2019 29-tissue atlas, the model predicts the substituted-to-reference abundance ratio from codon and sequence context; it says nothing about substitutions in undetectable peptides.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the protein sequence and codon around a residue to predict how much of the protein carries a non-genetic amino acid swap there.
plain_idea.train_on: Each detected substitution: the codon, the amino acid change, and the surrounding protein sequence; about 13,910 variants (7,215 unique) per the abstract, not counted in files.
plain_idea.predict: The ratio of substituted to normal peptide signal, measured by mass spectrometry in 29 healthy human tissues.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Translation-fidelity labs would learn whether error-prone sites follow simple codon rules or depend on protein context, and could pick sites to validate.

label_elsewhere.sources: Tsour et al. 2026 Nature (Slavov lab, decode.slavovlab.net, GitHub SlavovLab/decode; found by search); Mordret et al. 2019 Mol Cell (E. coli/yeast, PRIDE PXD014341; found by search).
label_elsewhere.why: A second human substitution set from another lab gives an external test of whether predicted hotspots replicate across pipelines.

risks: The same substitution measured in several tissues or individuals could land in both train and test.
Homologous proteins (paralogs, immunoglobulins) share near-identical windows across a split.
The ratio depends on reference peptide intensity, so protein abundance features can predict the label through detectability alone.
If the external Slavov set re-analysed the same raw files (PXD010154), it is not independent.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole genes, clustered at 30% sequence identity with MMseqs2; gene column not yet seen in files.
checks: Shuffle labels and confirm collapse to the per-substitution-type mean.
Train on reference peptide intensity alone to measure the detectability shortcut.
Check nearest-neighbour sequence identity of test windows to training windows.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable, but the detectability confound is a serious risk to interpretation.

success_criteria.metric: Spearman correlation between predicted and measured log10 ratio on held-out gene clusters, since the use is ranking sites to validate.
success_criteria.baselines: Per-substitution-type (codon to amino acid) mean ratio; per-gene mean; numbers not yet computed.
success_criteria.success: Spearman at least 0.10 above the per-substitution-type mean on held-out clusters, and positive transfer to the Tsour et al. set.
success_criteria.kill: ESM-2 features add under 0.05 Spearman over codon-type mean, or the supplement holds under 1,500 quantified unique substitutions.

ambitious.why: Publishes translation-fidelity analyses; would need a model whose predicted hotspots replicate across both labs' datasets.

realistic.why: Fits a cross-dataset re-analysis with a modest predictive model and harmonised substitution table.

fallback.why: A negative result (codon rules suffice, or sites don't replicate across pipelines) is still a useful note.

pitch.headline: Two independent 2026 Nature datasets of non-genetic human protein substitutions now exist, and nobody has tried to predict where they occur.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Per the abstract, 13,910 localized substitutions across 29 healthy tissues with substitution/reference abundance ratios; PRIDE deposit verified as CC0. Main table unopened (bioRxiv rate-limited).
pitch.the_win: A sequence model that ranks substitution hotspots on held-out genes and transfers to the Slavov lab's 8,746-site set with positive Spearman.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn how much the two labs' substitution calls overlap, and whether simple codon mismatch rules explain everything.
pitch.who_wants_it: Pilpel lab (Weizmann) and Slavov lab (Northeastern), deciding which substitution sites merit targeted validation.

ml_idea: Join substitutions with Ensembl protein sequences, embed a window around each site with ESM-2, add codon/near-cognate features, regress the log10 substitution ratio with gene-cluster CV, then test transfer to the Tsour et al. 2026 substitution set.

effort.compute_note: Estimated only: ~5,000 proteins with ESM-2 150M on CPU at ~1 protein/s; gradient boosting on ~10k rows; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Download the bioRxiv supplement zip and count unique quantified substitutions with a ratio and gene/position column; kill if under 1,500 or if no position/codon column.

verdict_reason: Likely novel prediction task with an independent second dataset, but the main variant table was not opened (bioRxiv returned HTTP 429), only detected substitutions exist (no clean negatives), and counts differ across filter stages.
